verdict.root_cause: cartservice is slow, not failing: traces show every cartservice server span consumed almost entirely by its own cache client spans (HGET/HMSET ~300-309ms each), giving ~300ms GetCart/EmptyCart and ~600ms AddItem, which propagates to frontend cart requests (~306ms GET, ~910ms POST) and checkout PlaceOrder (~660-680ms) while every other downstream leg is single- or low-double-digit ms. No error spans anywhere and frontend error ratio flat zero, consistent with a warning-severity latency incident. The failing mechanism is a slow cache dependency in cartservice's read/write path; the near-constant per-operation cost suggests a fixed configured/injected delay rather than organic contention, but no change record confirms this within the queried window.
verdict.reasoning: tr_8a248dc689c1 is the only dispatch that measured where time goes: cache client spans account for essentially the whole cartservice span, leaving negligible self-time, and it independently rules out productcatalog, shipping/quote, email, currency, payment, fraud and frontend/checkout orchestration as sources. tr_1c6bbccf1bb9 shows a defined, flat-zero frontend error ratio across all 61 points, so traffic was flowing and the symptom is latency rather than errors. tr_e1ff0d09fc2d (and tr_f2f149819e65) confirm cartservice was up and serving normal traffic at both ends of the window, excluding crash-loop. Change dispatches found nothing but cover only ~15 minutes, so they weaken bad_deploy without settling the origin. Per the taxonomy, delay inserted into a call path is classified by the wait, so dependency_latency; the fix is restoring normal cache call latency, most plausibly by reverting the setting that imposed it.
